items.headline: AI serving moves to production Kubernetes infrastructure
items.whatChanged: The llm-d distributed inference project reached v1.0, with maintainers saying open source AI serving is moving from experiments to production infrastructure [news-010]. Cloudflare also found that prompt caching dominated its AI review spend, making cache behavior a cost lever [news-003].
items.whyItMatters: Anthropic's Inference TPM role requires a working understanding of how LLM inference uses hardware [jd-tpm-001], and its Compute TPM role requires translating the needs of research or ML teams [jd-tpm-002]. Nuro's AI Platform TPM role also lists ML infrastructure experience as required [jd-tpm-004].

whatToDo.learn: This week, read the llm-d v1.0 announcement and write a one-page explainer of how an inference request uses GPU memory, batching, and caching, including where cost comes from.
whatToDo.resumeAngle: If you have worked with ML or infrastructure teams, write a bullet showing you coordinated delivery of an ML platform or serving project and tied technical tradeoffs such as cost or capacity to schedule decisions.
whatToDo.interviewQuestion: Walk me through how LLM inference uses hardware, and how that would shape the plan for a program launching a new model on shared GPU capacity.

items.headline: Launch playbooks get shadow testing and staged rollouts
items.whatChanged: Cloudflare ran its AI reviewer v1 and v2 side by side in shadow mode on canary repos before switching everyone to v2 [news-003]. Datadog added a Launches workflow that links launch planning, instrumentation, experimentation and reporting, with feature-flag rollouts that can start with employees or a small share of traffic [news-006].
items.whyItMatters: Ten of 16 job descriptions require this skill. Anthropic's Inference role asks you to own inference readiness for model launches [jd-tpm-001], and Nuro's role asks for coordinating release gates, rollout plans, and operational readiness [jd-tpm-004]. CoreWeave also requires operational readiness in large-scale infrastructure [jd-tpm-003].

whatToDo.learn: Draft a launch plan for a hypothetical feature with a tracking plan defined before release, a shadow or canary phase, feature-flag stages, and explicit go/no-go gates.
whatToDo.resumeAngle: If you have shipped anything, write a bullet that names the release gates you defined, the staged rollout you ran, and the result, such as issues caught before full exposure.
whatToDo.interviewQuestion: Describe how you would plan a staged rollout of a new model or platform change, including readiness criteria, canary approach, and rollback triggers.

items.headline: Agentic AI standards grow while security takes focus
items.whatChanged: The Agentic AI Foundation grew from three to ten projects in its first year [news-002]. MCP conference sessions shifted from new protocol features toward security and identity, and a speaker said agents have turned code review into the bottleneck [news-002].
items.whyItMatters: Few job descriptions ask for this yet, but Anthropic's Inference TPM role prefers building automations or agents [jd-tpm-001], and Scale AI's Red Team TPM role prefers familiarity with agentic misuse [jd-tpm-009]. That makes it an early mover chance for a candidate.

whatToDo.learn: Build a small agent workflow this week that uses an MCP server to automate one TPM task, such as summarizing status from tickets, and note how you would handle its permissions and identity.
whatToDo.resumeAngle: If you have automated any program workflow, write a bullet describing the manual process, the automation or agent you built, and the time saved or errors reduced, plus any access controls you set.
whatToDo.interviewQuestion: How would you introduce coding agents to an engineering team, and what would you do about review load and security risks?
